Article Title: Veeramani Pocso case: Photo of TVK minister with Gem Granites chief surfaces; DMK says 'take action'
Article Text:
Child rape: Granite baron Veeramani’s premises raided

SIT formed as probe expands

NEW DELHI: DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan hit back at allegations linking the party to Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani, saying the DMK should not be blamed for the alleged actions of an individual. His remarks came as Chennai police constituted a four-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe allegations of sexual offences against minor girls involving Veeramani.“They want to accuse the DMK for all those things. Today, there was a photograph on social media showing two ministers sitting with Veeramani. I don't understand anything,” Elangovan said.He added that Veeramani had been arrested and that the party leadership had also called for action if he was found to have committed any wrongdoing.“They have arrested him, and our leader also issued a statement that if he has committed a mistake, take action,” Elangovan said.Earlier, while talking to ANI, advocate and DMK leader NR Elango said "TN minister CTR Nirmal Kumar has falsely stated that the Veeramani case was diluted during the DMK regime. The case was registered on 07.12.2025 and investigated by the police. Houses were searched and further investigation was conducted based on the available evidence.The police had only stated that since adequate evidence was not yet available, complete investigation reports have not been filed so far, and that the further investigation is deferred until proper evidence is obtained—not that the case was dropped. The investigation was never dropped during the DMK regime."An SIT team has been formed as the investigation expands following the arrests of Veeramani and his associates.The SIT will be headed by Additional Commissioner of Police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch. Joint Commissioner of Police N Disha Mittal, Superintendent of Police Mutharasi and Deputy Commissioner of Police Geethanjali of the Central Women and Children unit are the other members of the team.Veeramani was arrested along with Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan on August 29 in connection with the POCSO case. A former Gem Granites employee, Ganesan, was subsequently arrested on September 22 after police allegedly found a video linked to the case on his mobile phone.Veeramani was arrested after a USB drive containing a video clip that purportedly showed a juvenile girl being sexually assaulted by him in Oct 2025. Police said they identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.
Article Summary: DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan hit back at allegations linking the party to Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani. He said the DMK should not be blamed for the alleged actions of an individual. His remarks came as Chennai police constituted a four-member Special Investigation Team to probe allegations.

Article Title: US mercenary, held at Myanmar camp, released from Tihar jail after NIA court's bail
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: US mercenary Aaron VanDyke, who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) earlier this year in the Myanmar terror training case, was released from the Tihar jail after after a special NIA court granted permission to travel to the USA to meet their families for one month.The NIA court, along with Matthew Aaron Vandyke, gave permission to 6 Ukrainian nationals to travel to Ukraine subject to certain conditions and formalities.The court directed the release of their passports to them. All 7 foreigners have been granted default bail by the court.While hearing the applications, the court noted that the accused had expressed their willingness to join the investigation whenever required by the NIA.The seven accused are Matthew Aaron Vandyke and co-accused Hurba Petro, Slyviak Taras, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Stefankiv Marian, Honcharuk Maksim alias Maksym and Kaminskyi Viktor.They have also been ordered to provide the NIA with their residential addresses, working mobile numbers and email addresses within 24 hours.If any of them does not have a working phone number, they may initially provide the mobile number of a family member.After reaching their respective destinations, they must provide their own working numbers within a week.Special Public Prosecutor Rahul Tyagi, along with advocate Amit Rohila, appeared for the NIA and told the court that further investigation was still under way.The agency submitted that the immediate presence of the accused was not required and said suitable undertakings could be obtained from them.Advocates Rohit Dandriyal and Rohit Gour appeared for Vandyke and also sought his discharge from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act following the compounding of those offences on September 18.The court allowed Vandyke's application for discharge from those offences.

Article Title: 'Must maintain the trust of people': Chirag Paswan urges EC to 'firmly present its side' amid SIR row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday urged the Election Commissioner to "firmly present its side" amid the ongoing row over the internal disagreements in the poll panel.Speaking to reporters, Chirag said the Election Commission must retain people's trust and address their doubts about the electoral process."If such questions are being raised against the Election Commission, I believe it is also the responsibility of the Election Commission, especially the CEC, to firmly present its side," the Union minister said."I don't care what the opposition says because it is their job is to do politics. The Election Commission must maintain the trust of the people because if doubts arise in the public's mind about the electoral process itself, that would be wrong. In such a situation, the Election Commission should firmly put forth its points so that no doubts arise in the people's minds," he added.This comes after the opposition demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation after an Indian Express report highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls.The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised formal objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period against decisions and orders related to electoral-roll processes.Earlier on Thursday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against the nation"."The Election Commission is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said, addressing a press conference.The Election Commission, however, described the queries and observations raised by its members as part of its routine internal process. It said written notes, technical inputs and internal scrutiny were standard mechanisms to check legal compliance and protect voters' rights.The ECI further said all decisions taken by the Commission, including those related to SIR, had full legal backing and stressed that its final decisions were unanimous.
Article Summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday urged the Election Commissioner to "firmly present its side" This comes after the opposition demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. An Indian Express report highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls.

NEW DELHI: A fresh landslide in Rimbi village under the Yuksom-Tashiding constituency of West Sikkim triggered a mudslide on Friday, sending large amounts of mud, rocks and debris downhill amid continued rainfall.The landslide has raised concerns among residents as nearby houses, properties and road connectivity remain at risk. Article Title: EC troika unanimously approved SIR orders on Forms 6 & 8, citizenship declaration: Officials
Article Text:

Election Commission officials Thursday said special intensive revision (SIR) orders related to Phase 1 in Bihar, Phase 2 in a dozen states/UTs and ongoing Phase 3 in 19 states/UTs had all listed Forms 6 and 8 with a mandatory declaration form on citizenship details of the elector or parents, and were unanimously approved by CEC and the two election commissioners.While Form 6 is an application for registration as a new elector, Form 8 is for shifting of an elector from outside the state/UT where he seeks to be enrolled.EC sources also denied ECINET was locking out field officers like electoral registration officers (EROs), assistant EROs, BLOs, DEOs, and chief electoral officers, saying ECINET is a decentralised platform designed in accordance with the RP Act 1950, RP Act 1951 and the instructions issued by EC from time to time.Citing the exact pages and paras of the orders, EC's clarification - which was reported exclusively in TOI Thursday - came amid a direct attack by Rahul Gandhi on CEC Gyanesh Kumar Thursday over alleged 'vote chori' and SIR anomalies, while praising the commissioners SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi for allegedly pointing out pitfalls in procedures adopted by EC for SIR of electoral rolls.It makes it clear that the SIR orders issued for Phase 1 in Bihar on June 24, 2025, for Phase 2 in a dozen states/UTs issued on Oct 27, 2025, and for Phase 3 in 19 states/UTs issued on May 14, 2026, were all unanimously approved by the three commissioners and that their objection to Form 6 and the declaration being unlawful and beyond the EC's remit was an afterthought.While Joshi had objected to Form 6 on May 16, two days after the third SIR order was signed by him, Sandhu did so on Aug 13, months after Supreme Court, in its verdict issued on SIR on May 27, 2026, upheld EC's power to add the declaration form.EC officials said the declaration form was introduced for the ease of voters so that whoever gives the declaration form need not submit any other documents. "This has been uniformly applied in SIR across all states/UTs," an EC official told TOI.On ECINET, the official said, "As per law, BLOs, AEROs, EROs, DEOs and CEOs can perform their statutory functions on this platform with their unique ID and password. Nobody else can perform their statutory function on it."
Article Summary: EC sources denied ECINET was locking out field officers like electoral registration officers (EROs), assistant EROs, BLOs, DEOs, and chief electoral officers. EC's clarification came amid a direct attack by Rahul Gandhi on CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged 'vote chori'

Article Title: SC flags ‘false’ POCSO cases in marital disputes, bars immediate arrest of accused parent
Article Text:
Rape-murder of A law student: Petitioner Ameer-Ul-Islam seeking transfer from Viyyur Central Prison in Kerala to a jail in Assam

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday laid down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act when the alleged offence involves a child living under the same roof and there is a matrimonial dispute between the child's parents.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan, flagging a rise in fakecases, said police should not act in haste in such cases and directed that, as a general rule, an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology should evaluate the child before authorities decide whether there is sufficient reason to arrest the accused.The court said the safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents. It stressed that the measures do not dilute the seriousness of offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, but are intended to ensure that the power of arrest is exercised after considering all relevant circumstances.The court said immediate arrest should not take place when two conditions are present: a POCSO offence is alleged against a parent or family member living with the child, and a matrimonial dispute exists between the child's parents, whether or not the dispute is pending before a court.The police officer receiving the complaint must verify whether such a matrimonial dispute exists, the court said. "When the above-stated threshold conditions are met, post the registration of an FIR, we are of the considered opinion that the investigating officer should not act in haste or take coercive actions in the form of arrest immediately," the bench added, as quoted by PTI.The verdict came in a matrimonial dispute involving an estranged Bengaluru couple. The wife had alleged that the child was sexually assaulted. The case was investigated by the CBI, which found the allegation to be false. The Supreme Court restored custody of the child to the father, taking into account the welfare of the minor.The court also directed the investigating officer or the Special Juvenile Police Unit to seek the services of an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology, in consultation with the District Child Protection Unit or, where one is unavailable, the District Legal Services Authority, adding that the expert's evaluation must be conducted independently and without influence from either the parent or investigating authorities.After receiving the evaluation, investigators must consider the expert's opinion along with other evidence and circumstances before deciding whether there is "reason to believe" that the accused committed the offence and whether an arrest is warranted. The court said an exception could be made in cases where the material available is "palpable", allowing the investigating officer to dispense with an expert evaluation, but reasons for doing so must be recorded in writing.The bench also stressed that arrest is not automatically required merely because an offence is cognisable. The court said an arrest can cause "irreparable harm" to an accused parent or family member, particularly where the allegation later turns out to be unfounded.The Supreme Court also raised concerns about the consequences of allegations on children and their relationship with the accused parent."The trauma that a child is put through in the process and the accusation can damage the very fabric of the parent-child relationship," the bench said, adding that such a wound could leave an "indelible scar" on both the child and parent.The court also flagged what it described as an increase in false allegations in matrimonial disputes."What is alarming is that this tendency of making false accusations is on the rise," it said.The bench cautioned against parents being influenced by advisers during matrimonial disputes, saying that some may be driven by a "win at any cost" approach.At the same time, the court said the safeguards were not a finding that allegations made in such circumstances are false. Investigating authorities must examine the allegations along with the surrounding circumstances and other evidence.For complaints filed directly before a special court, the Supreme Court said an order taking cognisance and summoning an accused must demonstrate application of mind. The special court should also involve an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology to evaluate the child and submit a report.
Article Summary: Supreme Court lays down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act. Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said police should not act in haste in such cases. The safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents.

Article Title: 'No trust in EC': Akhilesh Yadav alleges ‘vote theft’ in 2022 UP polls, says SP will contest 2027 in alliance
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav greets the crowd at the party's PDA Rath Yatra campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections, in Raebareli

Akhilesh links 2022 result to alleged 'vote theft'

SP says 2027 alliance will depend on winnability

Yadav attacks BJP over UCC, jobs and schools

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday accused the Election Commission of facilitating what he called "vote theft" of the PDA bloc in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, claiming that his party would have formed the government had the alleged irregularities not taken place.Addressing a public meeting in Raebareli after arriving on the party's specially designed PDA Rath, Yadav also said the SP would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in alliance, with seat-sharing based on the ability of a candidate or party to win."The Election Commission has been exposed and has worked like a puppet. Such a low level of work may never have happened in a democracy. Now, there is no trust in the Election Commission," Yadav said.The PDA acronym, coined by Yadav in 2023, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).Yadav alleged that the BJP was using the election machinery because it knew people would not vote for the party on issues such as inflation.He claimed that the alleged "vote theft" in the 2022 Assembly polls had prevented the SP from forming the government in Uttar Pradesh.The SP chief also attacked what he described as "bulldozer politics", saying the PDA movement would challenge it in the 2027 elections."This time (in 2027) the electoral verdict would not merely defeat them but would 'demolish' and permanently eliminate such negative politics," he said.Yadav also referred to the 2024 Lok Sabha election, saying, "We defeated them in 2024 and in 2027 we will work for their (BJP) permanent defeat."The SP and Congress had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Uttar Pradesh as allies, winning 37 and six seats respectively, for a combined tally of 43. The BJP won 33 seats in the state.Yadav said the SP would contest the 2027 polls as part of an alliance, although he did not specify its partners or the number of seats each party would contest."We will have an alliance," he said, adding that the basis for deciding seats would be winnability."Whoever can win a seat should get that seat," Yadav asserted.His remarks come as the SP and Congress face the question of whether they can maintain their alliance for the next Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.Yadav's PDA Rath campaign was launched from Raebareli, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is the sitting Lok Sabha MP. The SP had said Yadav's visit also included a planned meeting with Harchandpur MLA Rahul Lodhi, following a September 17 clash involving members of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha and ABVP.Police had denied allegations of manhandling by SP workers and said a magisterial inquiry into the police action had been ordered.The specially designed PDA Rath carries slogans including "Samajwadi PDA Yatra" and "PDA hi parivartan layega", along with the definition of PDA as Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak.Yadav also criticised the BJP over the alleged demolition of religious structures in Kashi and Saharanpur, accusing the party of pursuing communal politics and weakening social harmony.On the proposed Uniform Civil Code , he said laws should follow efforts to ensure equality among citizens."We say first make the citizens equal; first, let all of us become one. When everyone's respect becomes equal, then bring laws to increase that respect and take people forward," he said.On employment, Yadav promised that an SP government would increase government recruitment and provide jobs to young people."If outsourcing has to be ended, we will end outsourcing," he said.He also promised free treatment in hospitals, saying people would not have to search for a card before receiving healthcare.Yadav accused the state government of shutting primary schools while opening liquor shops and said an SP government would reopen schools that had been closed.He also promised to restore the old pension scheme for government employees.The Raebareli visit marks the beginning of the SP's PDA-focused outreach ahead of the 2027 Assembly election, with Yadav using the campaign to reiterate his allegations against the Election Commission, outline his alliance strategy and present the party's key electoral promises.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accuses Election Commission of facilitating what he called "vote theft" Yadav claims his party would have formed the government had alleged irregularities not taken place. Yadav also said the SP would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in alliance, with seat- sharing based on winnability.

Article Title: 'All elections rigged, laws illegal': Rahul Gandhi attacks Centre over EC-SIR row; BJP calls it 'jooth ki goonj'
Article Text:
File photo: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi

Rahul Gandhi demands CEC's resignation

What triggered the latest row?

BJP rejects Rahul's allegations

Rahul's anti-incumbency argument

NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday escalated his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that India's elections had been "rigged" and demanding the immediate resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress MP said Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar were "deshdrohis" (traitors) for what he alleged was the destruction of the country's vote.He said the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were "all rigged" and asserted that PM Modi and Shah would be investigated over what he described as a conspiracy to "steal elections".His remarks came a day after an investigation by a media report claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections to decisions and orders related to electoral-roll management and the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that these objections reflected a disagreement over its final decisions, saying its decisions, including those concerning SIR, were unanimous.Addressing a press conference at the Congress headquarters in New Delhi, Rahul said the Election Commission was responsible for protecting the vote and accused the poll panel of failing in that duty."Mr Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately. We are not going to let democracy be destroyed in India and sit silent, and the people responsible for this are going to be punished," Rae Bareli MP said.He said the reported objections by Sandhu and Joshi showed that questions were being raised within the poll panel itself."The two Election Commissioners have done a wise thing, and I appreciate it," he said.Former Congress president further alleged that the Prime Minister and home minister were "at the top of this conspiracy" and would be investigated. He also suggested that Kumar should "turn approver", describing that as an act of nationalism."I can say with certainty that Indian elections -- 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha polls -- were all rigged," Rahul said.He also linked the alleged manipulation of votes to the functioning of Parliament, laws and institutions."From vote chori (vote theft), comes kanoon chori (law theft) and from that comes sanstha chori (institutional theft)," he said.Explaining the argument, the Congress leader said the vote was the foundation of the constitutional system."If the vote has been destroyed, then our Constitution has been destroyed. If our Constitution has been destroyed, our laws are illegal. If our laws are illegal, our institutions are meaningless," he said.He said the alleged issue was therefore not limited to electoral rolls but concerned the wider constitutional framework."The central question here is this is not just an attack on the vote; this is an attack on the idea, the basic infrastructure, and the expression of every single Indian person," Rahul said.The immediate trigger was an Indian Express investigation reporting that Sandhu and Joshi recorded at least 14 objections over 10 months to decisions and orders issued in the name of the Election Commission.The objections reportedly covered voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 used for new voter registration, access to and centralisation of electoral-roll databases, and other aspects of the SIR exercise.The report said the two commissioners had objected four times on a single day and had raised concerns about decisions they said were taken without their knowledge or approval.The Election Commission, however, has disputed the interpretation that the reported internal notes amounted to a breakdown or disagreement over final decisions.The poll panel said internal technical notes, queries and suggestions were part of the normal administrative and decision-making process and maintained that the final decisions of the Commission were unanimous. Its response did not dispute the existence of the notes but said focusing on individual objections presented only part of the overall decision-making process.The EC's position is that all decisions relating to SIR had the approval of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sandhu and Joshi.The BJP hit back at Lok Sabha LoP's allegations, with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari describing his press conference as a "damp squib" and dubbing it "Jhoot Ki Goonj".In a post on X, Bhandari accused Rahul of making false claims and said the Congress leader was unable to win public support through democratic means.He also challenged Rahul's assertion that there had been no anti-incumbency against the BJP since 2014, saying the BJP had lost 20 elections since then.BJP leader and MP Sudhanshu Trivedi also challenged Rae Bareli MP's argument on anti-incumbency.He pointed to the Congress's electoral record in states including Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and argued that anti-incumbency had affected the Congress as well.On the media report, Trivedi questioned the basis for treating the reported objections as evidence that the Election Commission's final decisions were not unanimous."Do you have even a single report indicating that a decision was not unanimous?" Trivedi said, adding that there was no quoted statement from any Election Commissioner saying that a final decision had not been unanimous.He also questioned whether the reported internal objections should be treated as evidence of a wider institutional dispute when the Commission had maintained that its decisions were unanimous.A significant part of the Congress leader's press conference focused on what he described as the disappearance of anti-incumbency against the BJP.He cited electoral swings in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, and said governments and political parties in India had historically faced anti-incumbency."Haryana swings from one party to another for 50 years. Suddenly anti-incumbency disappears. Maharashtra swings; suddenly it disappears. Uttar Pradesh swings. Sometimes Samajwadi, sometimes BSP; it disappears. Madhya Pradesh, it disappears. Gujarat, it disappears," Rahul said.He cited former prime minister Indira Gandhi's experience after the 1971 Bangladesh war as an example of how anti-incumbency, according to him, had affected even highly popular leaders."It happens to leader after leader. It does not happen to PM Modi, Shah and the BJP - now we know the answer to it," he said.He also played videos of PM Modi and Shah, including remarks about the BJP remaining in power for decades and Modi's "Abki Baar 400 Paar" slogan. He argued that such statements were inconsistent with the normal operation of democratic politics.However, BJP has rejected Rahul's allegations, while the Election Commission has maintained that the reported objections were part of its internal decision-making process and that its final decisions, including those related to SIR, were unanimous.The dispute over the electoral-roll revision and the reported objections by the two election commissioners is now at the centre of the political exchange between Congress, BJP and the poll panel.
Article Summary: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi escalated his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Article Title: POCSO case cannot be quashed on settlement, says Delhi HC

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has held that proceedings under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cannot be quashed on the basis of a compromise between a child victim or the victim's family and the accused.Justice Sachin Datta made the observation while dismissing a petition seeking quashing of an FIR and related proceedings on the basis of a settlement allegedly reached with the victim with the intervention of her family, according to news agency ANI.The court noted that the case involved allegations of aggravated penetrative sexual assault against a child by a person allegedly in a position of trust or authority. It observed that such offences are heinous and have a serious impact on society.The high court relied on a Supreme Court judgment which held that while a high court has inherent powers to quash criminal proceedings in appropriate cases where parties have settled their dispute, such powers must be exercised after considering the nature and gravity of the offence.The Supreme Court has held that heinous and serious offences, including rape, ordinarily cannot be quashed merely because the victim or the victim’s family and the accused have reached a settlement, as such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.Applying the principle, the Delhi high court held that an offence under the POCSO Act cannot be compromised by the child victim or the victim’s family. It said quashing the proceedings at this stage on the basis of a compromise would defeat the object of the statute and the ends of justice.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court says POCSO offence cannot be quashed on basis of compromise. Case involved allegations of aggravated penetrative sexual assault against a child by a person allegedly in a position of trust or authority. High court relied on a Supreme Court judgment which held that while a high court has inherent powers to quash criminal proceedings in appropriate cases.

Article Title: The Backstory: When EC disagreements went public, from Seshan to Lavasa
Article Text:
From TN Seshan’s battle over the Election Commission’s structure to Ashok Lavasa’s dissent in 2019, the poll panel has seen internal disagreements emerge into the public domain.

When Seshan challenged other Election Commissioners

1995 verdict: CEC not above other ECs

2019: Lavasa's dissent

Ashok Lavasa resigned before he was made CEC.

'We are not clones': Sunil Arora

They should be included in final orders They should be discussed internally only They should be recorded but not affect the majority decision 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission is facing a fresh political storm over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, with the opposition demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation following a report in The Indian Express on differences within the poll panel over the exercise.According to the report, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times over 10 months to SIR-related decisions, including those concerning voter deletions and electoral roll data. The report has brought into focus a question that has surfaced at different points in the Election Commission's history: what happens when members of the poll panel disagree over how it should exercise its powers?There have been two prominent instances when such differences moved beyond the commission's internal proceedings and became matters of public and judicial scrutiny. In the 1990s, Chief Election Commissioner TN Seshan challenged the creation of a multi-member Election Commission and the appointment of two Election Commissioners alongside him. In 2019, Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa publicly dissented from the majority view on complaints alleging Model Code of Conduct violations by senior political leaders.TN Seshan was appointed Chief Election Commissioner in December 1990 and became known for his strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and his assertion of the Election Commission's constitutional powers.The structure of the commission changed in October 1993, when the government moved to make the poll panel a three-member body.On October 1, 1993, the President promulgated an ordinance providing for two Election Commissioners in addition to the CEC. On the same day, MS Gill and GVG Krishnamurthy were appointed as Election Commissioners. Seshan challenged the move in the Supreme Court, alleging that the appointments were intended to dilute his authority and "sideline" him. The government defended the move, maintaining that the Constitution permitted a multi-member Election Commission.The dispute soon spilled beyond the courtroom. The Supreme Court's eventual judgment recorded "unpleasant exchanges" between Seshan and Krishnamurthy at a meeting in October 1993, noting that allegations and counter-allegations had been made by the two commissioners. Gill later spoke publicly about the strained relationship, recalling his attempts to establish contact with Seshan after the appointments."The CEC, however, acted as if we don't exist," Gill famously said in 1995.Seshan approached the Supreme Court on October 26, 1993, challenging the ordinance and the appointments. The case raised a larger constitutional question: could the Chief Election Commissioner exercise overriding authority in a commission that now had two other members, or were all three meant to function collectively?The constitutional battle ended with a Supreme Court Constitution Bench judgment on July 14, 1995, which upheld the law providing for a multi-member Election Commission as well as the appointments of Gill and Krishnamurthy.The court rejected the proposition that the CEC's view would automatically prevail over those of the other Election Commissioners. "If the CEC is considered to be a superior in the sense that his word is final, he would render the ECs non-functional or ornamental," the court observed.The judgment also commented on the personal friction that had accompanied the constitutional dispute. "It is a pity they did not try to work as a team," the court said, adding that "suspicion and distrust got the better of them", while expressing the hope that the commissioners would work with mutual respect and confidence.The verdict thus established the framework for the functioning of a multi-member Election Commission, making clear that the CEC could not treat the other Election Commissioners as subordinate members whose views could simply be overridden.More than two decades later, another disagreement within the Election Commission became public during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. The commission then comprised CEC Sunil Arora and Election Commissioners Ashok Lavasa and Sushil Chandra, with Lavasa disagreeing with the majority view in several complaints alleging Model Code violations by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah.The majority gave PM Modi and Shah clean chits in the complaints, while Lavasa wanted his dissenting views to be recorded and included in the commission's orders. The disagreement subsequently became a dispute over whether a minority opinion should form part of the final order issued by the poll panel.Lavasa eventually informed Arora that he would stay away from proceedings concerning MCC complaints. In a letter, he said his minority decisions were being "suppressed" in a manner contrary to conventions followed by multi-member statutory bodies and wrote: "In the present circumstances, I am left with no option but to keep away from such proceedings."The dispute became public during the election campaign, prompting then CEC Sunil Arora to respond. On May 18, 2019, Arora said the three members of the Commission were not expected to agree on every issue."The three members of ECI are not expected to be template or clones of each other," Arora said, describing the controversy as "unsavoury and avoidable". He also noted that differences of opinion had existed within the Commission in the past.The full Commission subsequently discussed how dissent should be recorded. Lavasa's demand that minority views be made part of the final MCC orders was not accepted. Instead, the commission decided that the views of all members would be recorded in its proceedings, while the final order would reflect the majority decision.On August 18, 2020, Lavasa resigned as Election Commissioner after being appointed vice-president of the Asian Development Bank. He had joined the Election Commission in January 2018 and still had more than two years left in his tenure. He was also next in line to become Chief Election Commissioner.The Election Commission formally bid farewell to Lavasa later that month, with Arora saying the ECI's loss was the Asian Development Bank's gain.
Article Summary: In the 1990s, Chief Election Commissioner TN Seshan challenged the creation of a multi-member Election Commission. In 2019, Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa publicly dissented from the majority view on complaints alleging Model Code of Conduct violations. The Election Commission is facing a fresh political storm over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

What is the criminal conduct? The Election Commission is made up of three Election Commissioners to maintain checks and balances. Majority decisions prevail. It has now been proven by the Indian Express investigative report yesterday that two of the three Election Commissioners, namely Mr Joshi and Mr Sandhu, dissented from Mr Gyanesh Kumar's actions on 14 occasions in the last 10 months, and sometimes as many as four times in a single day," Mahua said."Very important things, such as the centralisation of the IT software, were left entirely in the hands of DG IT Seema Khanna, who was using this software to bypass local, on-ground officials. How does a new voter get enrolled by filling out Form 6? What Gyanesh Kumar did illegally was insert a new question into Form 6, which is: Are you or any of your parents or grandparents linked to the SIR, yes or no? Mr Sandhu and Mr Joshi dissented and said that only by amending the rules could you do this; you cannot simply add a question," she said."Nobody could answer. The CEO of West Bengal could not answer, and the Chief Election Commissioner could not answer, and lakhs and crores of new voters were left out. Today, all over India, 13 crore voters have been deleted. What will happen to their children? What will happen to their children when they turn 18? They cannot get on the rolls either. So this is criminal conduct, and they cannot hide behind Section 16 of the CEC and EC Act of 2023," she added.Later, after filing the FIR, Mahua shared a post on X along with a copy of the complaint. "Gyanesh Chor Kumar is rogue agent who acted without consent of other 2 ECs. Disenfranchising genuine voters is not official duties. He cannot enjoy immunity. He needs to be prosecuted. Simple," she wrote on X.According to the media report, the two Election Commissioners had objected to changes in Form 6, with Joshi and Sandhu recording that the statutory form could not be altered without amending the relevant rules. Sandhu later described the changes as “unauthorised and illegal” and called for their immediate removal.The ECI has maintained that written notes, observations and internal checks are part of normal institutional deliberations. It has also said that its official orders and decisions have full legal sanction and that final decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously.The reported objections relate to voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 and centralised control of the electoral-roll database. According to the report, the two commissioners also raised concerns about access to the electoral-roll database by statutory officials.The reported differences have triggered demands from Opposition parties for action against Kumar. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that the BJP, RSS and the Election Commission had committed an act of “treason” through what he called “vote chori”."Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our Constitution," Rahul said. "The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served."Mamata Banerjee also alleged that the BJP and the EC had “looted” the West Bengal Assembly polls and demanded fresh elections in the state using the voter list that existed before the SIR.Meanwhile, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra defended the Election Commission, saying differences and exchanges between commissioners reflected “pure democracy” and were part of institutional deliberations.
Article Summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra filed a police complaint against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. She alleged that Kumar and the Election Commission's IT system had bypassed local officials responsible for maintaining electoral rolls.
