Safeguard for working landscapes and wildlife

The largest remaining intact part of an 1843 Mexican land grant in California's Cuyama Valley has been permanently protected from future commercial development after a successful grassroots conservation campaign. The 5,650-acre Spanish Ranch, managed by the Doiron family, is now protected by a permanent agricultural conservation easement through a partnership with the California Rangeland Trust. The agreement guarantees that the historic cattle ranch will remain working agricultural land forever, preventing future subdivisions or industrial development. The agreement was completed after a $1 million fundraising campaign. It protects important wildlife corridors, native oak forests, and headwater habitats across San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties. According to an official announcement from the California Rangeland Trust, the project protects a continuous farming and ranching tradition that began before California became a state.The property is the main part of what was originally called Rancho Cuyama (No. 1), a 22,193-acre land grant awarded in 1843 by Mexican Governor Manuel Micheltorena to José María Rojo.After the Mexican-American War ended and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was signed in 1848, the United States government formally recognized the land grant. Over the past 183 years, large parts of California's historic ranchos have been divided into smaller residential lots, farmland, and industrial sites. Spanish Ranch remains the largest connected parcel from the original 1843 grant that is still being used for agriculture. The Doiron family bought the land decades ago and has operated it as a traditional cattle ranch while preserving its open natural spaces. As development pressure increased in the Cuyama Valley, the family began working with conservation groups to protect the property permanently. In a statement released by the California Rangeland Trust, landowner Pam Doiron spoke about the property's deep historical importance. "The ranch is a symbol that shows that agriculture, history, and conservation go hand in hand," Doiron said. "I am proud, along with my family, to carry that legacy forward."Protecting the land required funding from several sources, including federal grants, charitable foundations and individual donors. Federal funding came from the US Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service through its Agricultural Conservation Easement Program, which provides matching funds to protect working agricultural land. The California Rangeland Trust raised the remaining money through a $1 million fundraising campaign. More than 140 private donors and seven charitable foundations contributed to the campaign, providing nearly 54% of the project’s total funding. A major leadership grant from the John S. Kiewit Memorial Foundation provided the final amount needed to complete the project. According to California Rangeland Trust records, the organisation now protects more than 150,000 acres of working land across Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties. That accounts for 34% of its conservation portfolio across California. During a dedication ceremony, Eric Hvolboll, board president of the John S. Kiewit Memorial Foundation, said supporting conservation agreements for working land closely matched the region’s conservation goals.Beyond its historical value, Spanish Ranch provides an important natural buffer between the Los Padres National Forest and the Cuyama River basin. The property offers important habitat for native wildlife, including the California condor, tule elk, pronghorn, and several species of special concern. Under the legal agreement, the Doiron family keeps full private ownership and control of the cattle ranch. However, the easement permanently removes all future commercial development rights. This ensures that the soil, watershed, and vegetation can remain protected. Michael Delbar, Chief Executive Officer of the California Rangeland Trust, pointed to the wider importance of the agreement for protecting land in the region. "Spanish Ranch represents what is possible when landowners, conservation partners, and communities come together around a shared vision for the future," Delbar stated. "We are not just conserving acres, we are helping ensure that these working landscapes remain whole, productive, and connected for generations to come."
Article Summary: The 5,650-acre Spanish Ranch in California's Cuyama Valley is protected by a permanent agricultural conservation easement. The agreement guarantees that the historic cattle ranch will remain working agricultural land forever. It protects important wildlife corridors, native oak forests, and headwater habitats across San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties.

Article Title: Texas homeowner Elizabeth Luna wins $33,243 after nearly 3-year HOA battle over rental ban, tenant interference and blocked property sale; HOA ordered to pay $20,743, president Terri Thomure $12,500
Article Text:
Elizabeth Luna won $33,243 after a nearly three-year legal battle with her Texas HOA over rental restrictions and property rights. (Photo: KSAT 12)

HOA changed rental rules after Luna bought property

Tenant allegedly backed out after HOA confrontation

A Bexar County judge ordered the Oaks Northwest HOA to pay $20,743.39, while its president Terri Thomure was ordered to pay $12,500. (Photo: KSAT 12)

Court orders HOA and president to pay

Luna says homeowners should hold boards accountable

HOA disputes continue to draw attention

A Texas homeowner has won more than $33,000 in damages, attorney’s fees and other awards after a nearly three-year legal battle with her homeowners association over rental restrictions, tenant interference and an attempt to block the sale of her property.Elizabeth Luna, who owned a rental townhome in the Oaks Northwest community near the San Antonio Medical Center, prevailed in a Bexar County court case against the HOA and its president, Terri Thomure. The case, reported by KSAT, centered on a dispute that began after the association moved to restrict short-term rentals.Luna purchased the townhome when there were no restrictions preventing her from renting it out, according to the report.That changed in 2023 when HOA President Terri Thomure pushed for a ban on short-term rentals in the 11-unit community. Luna challenged the change, alleging that a special meeting held in March 2023 did not comply with notice requirements under Texas law.Luna argued that the procedural issue made the amendment invalid.Despite the new restrictions, Luna said she attempted to comply with the association’s rules by securing a tenant under a 12-month lease.The dispute escalated when, according to Luna’s lawsuit, Thomure approached the tenant’s assistant in the community’s parking lot.Luna alleged that Thomure did not identify herself and demanded to know who the woman was and why she was at the property. Luna told KSAT that the interaction was unsettling and that the tenant subsequently terminated the lease.The dispute later extended to Luna’s attempt to sell the townhome.After Luna put the property on the market, the HOA filed a legal claim against the home that prevented the sale from proceeding, she told the station. A judge later dismissed the claim, allowing Luna to complete the sale in May 2024.Luna continued pursuing the case even after selling the property.In May 2026, a judge in Bexar County’s 438th District Court ruled in her favor. The Oaks Northwest HOA was ordered to pay Luna $10,743.39 in damages and $10,000 in attorney’s fees, while Thomure was separately ordered to pay $12,500 for interfering with Luna’s rental contract.The combined judgments total $33,243.39.Luna told KSAT that both judgments have been paid.Reflecting on the nearly three-year dispute, Luna said her goal was to demonstrate that homeowners have options when they believe an HOA board is abusing its authority or failing to follow applicable rules.“What was going through my head when all of this was happening is the abuse of power of the homeowners association,” Luna told KSAT.She said the lengthy legal fight ultimately showed her that homeowners should not be afraid to challenge decisions they believe are improper.“If you find that your board members are not following the rules, hold them accountable,” Luna said. “Hold them to a higher standard.”Luna’s case highlights the disputes that can arise between homeowners and associations over rental restrictions, property sales and the authority of HOA boards.HOAs can establish and enforce rules affecting properties within their communities, but their actions remain subject to governing documents and applicable state laws. In Luna’s case, the court proceedings ultimately resulted in financial judgments against both the association and its president.
Article Summary: Elizabeth Luna won $33,243 after a nearly three-year legal battle with her Texas HOA. The case centered on a dispute that began after the association moved to restrict short-term rentals. The dispute later extended to Luna’s attempt to sell the townhome.

Article Title: In 1888, George Vanderbilt began building a vast North Carolina estate; 26 years later, his widow sold 86,700 acres for $433,500, helping create the core of Pisgah National Forest in 1916
Article Text:
Building a cradle of forestry

Anchoring public land conservation

Enduring environmental heritage

A major property deal that began more than a century ago with a grieving widow turned a huge private wilderness in North Carolina into one of the most important public conservation achievements in American history. In May 1914, Edith Vanderbilt agreed to sell 86,700 acres of valuable mountain forest from the private Biltmore Estate to the United States federal government for $433,500. The deal was made at $5.00 per acre and moved the huge forest area into public ownership. The land later became the foundation of Pisgah National Forest, which was formally established in 1916. The sale carried out the conservation plan of her late husband, George Washington Vanderbilt. He began buying worn-out farmland and mountain slopes near Asheville, North Carolina, in 1888. Over 26 years, he collected more than 125,000 acres to build a self-sufficient mountain retreat centered around the 250-room Biltmore House.When George Vanderbilt first bought land in Western North Carolina, years of uncontrolled logging and burning had badly damaged local watersheds and forests. To restore the land, Vanderbilt hired famous landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted and young forestry expert Gifford Pinchot, who later became the first chief of the United States Forest Service.Under their direction, the Biltmore property became a testing ground for scientific forest management and soil restoration across the American South. In 1898, German forester Carl A. Schenck founded the Biltmore Forest School on the estate. It became the first school of professional forestry in North America. After George Vanderbilt unexpectedly died in March 1914 from complications following surgery, keeping the huge private property became a major financial burden for his widow. Edith Vanderbilt chose to follow her husband's wish to preserve the mountain wilderness instead of selling the land to commercial timber companies. According to historical records documented by the Forest History Society, Edith wrote directly to United States Secretary of Agriculture David F. Houston on 1 May 1914 to formally offer the land to the federal government. In her letter, she explained that she wanted the land protected for the public. She wrote: "I wish to sell this tract of land to the Government at a price significantly below its commercial value in order that my husband's plan for the protection of these mountain forests may be permanently realized."The purchase was made possible by the Weeks Act, a federal law passed by the United States Congress in 1911. The law allowed the federal government to buy private land in eastern states to protect the headwaters of navigable rivers and manage forest resources. The National Forest Reservation Commission, led by Secretary Houston, quickly approved the deal. Official commission records kept in the Forest History Society archives show that the government considered the $5.00-per-acre price an exceptional bargain. Private timber companies had offered much more for the right to cut down the forests. The transaction was completed in 1914. Only 10,000 acres around the main Biltmore House and its immediate grounds remained in private family ownership. On 17 October 1916, President Woodrow Wilson issued an executive proclamation creating Pisgah National Forest, with the former Vanderbilt land serving as its central area.The purchase protected important headwater areas for major river systems in the region, including the French Broad River basin. Today, Pisgah National Forest covers more than 500,000 acres across the Appalachian Mountains. Millions of people visit the forest each year for hiking, scientific research, and wildlife conservation. The birthplace of American forestry is still preserved within the forest at the Cradle of Forestry in America National Historic Site. The site stands on the same grounds where Schenck's students once attended their original field lectures. By accepting a much lower price for the land, Edith Vanderbilt protected both the financial future of the remaining estate and a large area of North American wilderness for future generations. The deal remains one of the largest single land purchases made under the Weeks Act and helped set an example for protecting public land across the eastern United States.
Article Summary: In 1914, Edith Vanderbilt agreed to sell 86,700 acres of valuable mountain forest to the United States federal government for $433,500. The sale carried out the conservation plan of her late husband, George Washington Vanderbilt. The land later became the foundation of Pisgah National Forest, which was formally established in 1916.

Article Title: Bihar shocker: After Jamui, Samastipur, another girl harassed in public at tourist site
Article Text:
Image Credit: X

Video shows group surrounding girl at Mandar Parvat

Police suspect video may be six months old

FIR against six unidentified youths

Samastipur video leads to four arrests

One arrested in Muzaffarpur case

Police dismiss Madhepura video claim

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most important factor in tackling public harassment? Stronger laws and penalties Awareness campaigns Community involvement and support 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PATNA: A video allegedly showing a minor girl being harassed in public at Bihar’s Mandar Parvat tourist site in Banka has surfaced online, prompting police to register a case against six unidentified youths.The development comes days after separate molestation and sexual assault cases in Jamui and Samastipur sparked concern over law and order in the state.The video, allegedly recorded at the tourist site under Bounsi police station, shows a group of youths allegedly misbehaving with the girl. One youth appears to twist her arm, while another attempts to hit her with a slipper. A third is seen carrying a stick.The clip has been edited with a song that appears to glorify hooliganism and has been widely circulated on social media.Although the video carries a September 3 date, police said preliminary findings suggest the footage could be around six months old.Investigators are now trying to establish when the incident actually took place and verify the circumstances in which the video was recorded.Bounsi SHO Pankaj Kumar Jha said the social media cell received the video through WhatsApp on September 22. A police team later visited the location and found that the footage appeared to have been shot at Mandar Parvat.Police have registered a suo motu FIR against six unidentified youths under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act.Bounsi SDPO Indrajit Baitha said efforts were underway to identify those seen in the video and that further legal action would follow based on the investigation.The Banka case comes days after a separate video from Samastipur allegedly showed a girl being harassed in public.Police arrested four people in connection with that case and booked them under relevant provisions of the BNS, IT Act and POCSO Act.According to Samastipur police, the video appeared to be about a week old and the victim had not yet been identified. Police said a case was registered because the girl appeared to be a minor and the matter was considered sensitive.The arrested men were identified as Vikas Kumar, Rahul Kumar and Rambabu Sahni, residents of Jagatsinghpur village, where the incident allegedly occurred, and Awadhesh Paswan, a resident of Bijaulia.In neighbouring Muzaffarpur, police arrested Lalit Kumar for allegedly molesting and beating a girl in the Town police station area.Police said the accused appeared to be mentally unstable and that his condition was being assessed by experts. The girl was admitted to Sadar Hospital for treatment.Police also rejected claims circulating on social media about a similar incident in Madhepura.According to Madhepura police, the video was recorded near a secondary school and showed male and female students involved in a heated argument after their half-yearly examinations.The recent cases have drawn political attention, with the opposition targeting the BJP-led NDA government over the law and order situation in Bihar.
Article Summary: Video allegedly shows group surrounding girl at Mandar Parvat tourist site. Police suspect video may be six months old.FIR against six unidentified youths has been registered. Comes days after separate molestation and sexual assault cases in Jamui and Samastipur.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay delays tests as faculty calls for 'student-friendly' SOP on handling exam misconduct
Article Text:
IIT-Bombay has postponed mid-semester exams to allow time for a committee to create guidelines





MUMABAI: IIT-Bombay has po­stponed a set of mid-sem­ester exams to give a committee time to frame an SOP and revise rules to han­dle academic misconduct.Last Saturday, a profess­or was named in an FIR by the par­ents of a 2nd-year student who committed suicide.Faculty members have demanded a clear standard operating procedure (SOP) that spells out, step by step, how invigilators should deal with students suspected of exam malpractice. The tests sched­u­led for Sept 26-27 will now be held on Oct 10-11, with the tim­etable remaining unchanged, stud­ents were told Thursday.A communication sent by Siddhant Gupta, general sec­retary, academic affairs (UG), said the postponement is intended to give the new comm­ittee, which has equal student representation, time to draw up a “clear and student-frie­ndly” SOP for invigilators and revise the rules govern­ing academic misconduct.The move assumes significance amid the debate on how students accused of exam violations are dealt with on campus and whether existing procedures leave too much discretion to individual faculty members or invigilators.Faculty members have specifically emphasised the need for detailed instructi­ons on how examinations are to be conducted and how suspected cases of misconduct should be handled. The proposed SOP is expected to lay down the procedure to be followed at every stage, from the point at which an invigilator suspects a violation to the subsequent action against the student.“Faculty have emphasised the need for clear, step-by-step instructions on conducting examinations and handling incidents of suspected academic misconduct, including the procedure and actions to be followed at each stage,” the letter said.The institute has said the objective is to ensure that examinations are conducted in a fair and consistent manner, while also giving due consideration to students’ concerns. Student stakeholders were consulted before the exams were postponed, the communication said.The revised SOP and academic misconduct rules will not come into force immediately. These will first be placed before the IIT-B senate for approval, said the letter sent to campus residents. “The exercise could lead to a more standardised framework for dealing with suspected examination violations, particularly by defining what an invigilator can do at the examination hall, what must be documented, and what procedure should follow before further disciplinary action is taken,” said a civil engineering faculty member of IIT-B.
Article Summary: IIT-Bombay has postponed mid-semester exams to allow time for a committee to create guidelines. Last Saturday, a profess­or was named in an FIR by the par­ents of a 2nd-year student who committed suicide.Faculty members have demanded a clear standard operating procedure.

Article Title: Police head constable Nitin shot dead by son at his Chandigarh residence
Article Text:
Head constable Nitin shot dead by son at Chandigarh home.





CHANDIGARH: A Chandigarh Police head constable was found dead with a gunshot injury to his head at his government accommodation in Sector 22 on Friday morning, with police investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Deceased son Arman is the main suspect behind the murder. Police rounded up Arman and interrogating him.The deceased was identified as Nitin, who was posted in the Accounts Branch at the Chandigarh police headquarters in Sector 9. His wife is also posted as an ASI with Chandigarh police.According to preliminary information, Nitin, his wife and their son were present at the house when the incident took place. Around 7 am, the head constable’s wife reportedly went to the terrace and raised an alarm, following which neighbours gathered at the spot.When people entered the house, Nitin was found lying on a bed in a pool of blood. He had sustained a serious gunshot injury to his head. Police said the circumstances leading to the firing were yet to be established.A country-made pistol was recovered from the spot. Police teams are examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area and questioning family members, including the couple’s son, as part of the investigation.On receiving information, Chandigarh Police SSP Kanwardeep Kaur, SP Crime Anurag Daru and station house officers of police stations under the Central Division reached the spot. The officers inspected the government accommodation and the scene of the incident.Police are investigating whether the firing was accidental, self-inflicted or involved any other circumstances. Further details are awaited as the investigation is underway
Article Summary: Chandigarh Police head constable was found dead with a gunshot injury to his head at his government accommodation in Sector 22. Deceased son Arman is the main suspect behind the murder. Police are investigating whether the firing was accidental, self-inflicted or involved any other circumstances.

Article Title: Twist in Kanpur bizman’s murder probe: Son held, no ‘clean chit’ to bahu yet
Article Text:
Police Subrat (34), alleging he masterminded the conspiracy, hired two assassins and instructed them to name his wife Shalu if the plot was uncovered.





KANPUR: In a dramatic turnaround in the investigation into the murder of 63-year-old pharmaceutical trader Vineet Minocha, police have arrested his son, Subrat (34), alleging that he masterminded the conspiracy and hired two men to carry out the killing.Police said the investigation so far has not found corroborative evidence against Subrat’s wife, Shalu (30), who had earlier been arrested in the case. However, officers stressed that she has not been given a clean chit yet.Kanpur police commissioner Raghubir Lal told TOI that the investigating officer, inspector KK Tiwari, would submit a report before the court incorporating all evidence, including details emerging from the interrogation of Vineet’s former employee Vishal Gautam, one of the accused.Sources said investigators were still scrutinising the call records between Shalu and Vishal—25 calls on her old number and seven on the new one—as well as her alleged instruction to the gatekeeper to keep the gate open on the day of the murder.DCP (west) Qasim Abidi said the investigation and court proceedings had been affected for some time due to protests by lawyers, which created a roadblock in the case.A senior police officer said Shalu’s alleged role, if any, would ultimately be determined on the basis of evidence and by the court.“Whether she is complicit or not will be decided by the court,” the officer said.Police on Thursday said Subrat had hired Vishal and Raj Kishor to carry out the killing. Investigators said Subrat wanted to eliminate the hurdles his father was allegedly creating for his lavish lifestyle. Police said Subrat was deeply involved in IPL betting, gambling and intoxicants and had accumulated debts of more than Rs 40 lakh.According to the investigation, Subrat received Rs 40,000 a month from his father, but paid about Rs 55,000 monthly towards debt instalments. He allegedly took medicines from the shop and sold them through Vishal to raise money.Police said Subrat feared his father might marry another woman and transfer his movable and immovable property to her.Vishal and Raj were earlier arrested following a police encounter. Shalu was also arrested after the two accused named her during questioning. However, police said evidence subsequently indicated that Subrat had instructed them to name his wife if the conspiracy was uncovered.Investigators cited CCTV footage, call detail records, scientific evidence and recoveries made during the accused’s police custody. Police recovered a duplicate key to Vineet’s flat at Vishal’s instance and blood-stained clothes allegedly worn during the crime from near Central Railway Station at Raj’s instance.The person who made the duplicate key identified Vishal. The role of Subrat has come under the scanner after police found that he allegedly refused to identify the contract killers despite having spoken to Vishal nearly 300 times in the three months before the murder. Investigators suspect Subrat deliberately withheld the identification to distance himself from the alleged conspiracy.WhatsApp chats between Subrat and Vishal had also been deleted from their phones, while Vishal had obtained a new SIM three days before the murder.Police initially said Shalu had provided the flat key. Detailed investigation and call record analysis allegedly showed that Subrat had paid Vishal to have a duplicate key made. Police said evidence did not corroborate Shalu’s involvement and indicated that Subrat alone hatched the conspiracy.A Kanpur Nagar chief judicial magistrate granted police custody of the accused from noon on Sept 23 to noon on Sept 24 for recoveries, questioning and evidence collection.During questioning, Vishal reportedly told police that he had worked at Vineet’s shop before being dismissed about five years ago, but remained in contact with Subrat.
Article Summary: Police have arrested his son, Subrat (34), alleging that he masterminded the conspiracy and hired two men to carry out the killing. Police said the investigation so far has not found corroborative evidence against Subrat’s wife, Shalu (30)

Article Title: Not all facial pains akin to actor Salman Khan’s condition, say doctors
Article Text:
Kamla Devi, Geeta Pandey, Dr Sujeet Gautam and actor Salman Khan

Lucknow:





For a long time, Rae Bareli’s Kamla Devi (45) and Ayodhya’s Geeta Pandey (51) believed they had trigeminal neuralgia—the agonising condition that had afflicted megastar Salman Khan . But when they reached SGPGI’s Pain Clinic, doctors found that their excruciating, shock-like facial pain was not trigeminal neuralgia but was caused by pinched nerves in the neck.For both women, the pain had meant years of misdiagnoses, repeated hospital visits, failed treatments and mounting despair. Kamla had even undergone surgery, but it brought her no relief. Geeta, too, lived with persistent facial pain that affected her daily life.At SGPGI, specialists found their symptoms, though similar to trigeminal neuralgia, were caused by overlapping facial-pain syndromes originating from irritated or trapped nerves in the neck. The distinction was crucial because treating the trigeminal nerve would not have addressed the actual source of their pain.Doctors used precise, minimally invasive techniques to treat the problem. Hydrodissection was performed to free trapped nerves and muscles in the neck, while targeted radiofrequency lesioning was used to calm overactive nerve clusters by applying controlled, mild heat.Both women experienced lasting relief and were able to return to their normal lives without undergoing open surgery.The cases highlight the diagnostic challenge posed by facial pain, which can have several causes and may produce similar symptoms. Doctors at the Pain Clinic said patients with persistent facial pain may need a fresh assessment when conventional treatment fails, rather than repeating the same approach.“These cases remind that overlapping facial-pain syndromes can seem alike but come from different nerves — and the diagnosis, not just the treatment, determines whether a patient gets better,” said Dr Sujeet Gautam, professor at the Pain Clinic, SGPGI. “When pain persists, we must step back and reassess rather than repeat the same approach.”
Article Summary: Kamla Devi (45) and Geeta Pandey (51) believed they had trigeminal neuralgia. The agonising condition had afflicted megastar Salman Khan. When they reached SGPGI’s Pain Clinic, doctors found that their excruciating, shock-like facial pain was caused by pinched nerves in the neck.

Article Title: 7-year-old girl dies after collapsing in class amid loud DJ procession in UP; 2 arrested
Article Text:
Girl, 7, dies after collapsing in Balrampur classroom amid loud DJ music; 2 held





LUCKNOW: Balrampur police on Wednesday night arrested a DJ owner and an operator after a seven-year-old student died allegedly because of loud DJ music being played near her school during a Ganesh idol immersion procession on Tuesday.Police arrested Chandra Prakash Verma, owner of Balaji Hightech DJ, and Rampal Saini, the DJ operator, while Shailendra Kumar Yadav, in charge of Mewalal police outpost, was suspended. Santosh Mishra, Kotwali Nagar inspector, was also issued a show-cause notice for negligence.An FIR was registered at Kotwali Nagar police station on the complaint of school manager Ashish Kumar Upadhyay, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 223 (disobedience to public servant) of BNS.Police also seized the pickup vehicle, the DJ sound system and other equipment allegedly used during the procession.A senior police officer said the deceased was attending classes as usual when she collapsed at around 10.58 am. Teachers immediately attended to her. She briefly regained her posture but collapsed again shortly afterwards and did not respond to attempts to revive her. She was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared her dead.At the time of the incident, a Ganpati immersion procession was passing near the school with a DJ system. A teacher, Ikra Khan, told investigators that the DJ sound had intensified and vibrations could be felt inside the classroom around the time Vaishnavi fell ill.Police are scanning the CCTV footage from the classroom to establish the sequence of events.However, police have not established that the DJ sound caused the girl’s death. The child was not subjected to a post-mortem examination, making it difficult to medically determine the exact cause of death.Following the incident, police held a meeting with DJ operators and directed them not to play DJs after 10 pm, avoid excessive use of heavy bass and refrain from using unusually tall DJ setups.Police said excessive noise can adversely affect children, the elderly, patients and students.
Article Summary: Girl, 7, dies after collapsing in Balrampur classroom amid loud DJ music; 2 held. Police arrested Chandra Prakash Verma, owner of Balaji Hightech DJ, and Rampal Saini, the DJ operator. Shailendra Kumar Yadav, in charge of Mewalal police outpost, was suspended.

Article Title: IPL bets, affairs, loans, lavish lifestyle: Killer 'son' emerges from shadows as Kanpur bizman murder case takes major twist
Article Text:
Subrat Minocha, a 34-year-old man, has been arrested for allegedly conspiring to murder his father, Vineet Minocha.





KANPUR: IPL betting, mounting loans, a lavish lifestyle and a fear that his father’s property could go to another woman — investigators say these strands came together in the alleged plot to kill 63-year-old pharmaceutical trader Vineet Minocha.Police have now arrested his 34-year-old son Subrat, alleging that he masterminded the conspiracy and hired two men to carry out the murder.Police alleged that Subrat had accumulated debts of more than Rs 40 lakh through gambling and IPL betting and was also involved in intoxicants.According to investigators, Subrat received around Rs 40,000 every month from his father for his expenses but was paying about Rs 55,000 a month towards loan instalments. Police said his father had become an obstacle to the lifestyle Subrat wanted to maintain.Another strand of the alleged motive was Vineet’s personal life. Police said Subrat feared that his father, who had strained relations with his current wife, might marry another woman and transfer his property to her. Vineet’s wife was staying with their daughter outside Uttar Pradesh, investigators said.Police alleged that Subrat therefore decided to get his father killed.According to investigators, the original plan was to make Vineet’s death appear accidental or natural, but it was later changed. Vishal Gautam, a former employee of Vineet, allegedly agreed to carry out the killing with the help of his associate Rajkishore.Vineet was stabbed 26 times at his Ratan Orbit apartment in Kanpur’s Kalyanpur area on September 5. Police said Vishal and Rajkishore entered the flat posing as medicine delivery men before attacking him and later escaped by scaling a wall.The two men were arrested shortly after the murder and subsequently named Vineet’s daughter-in-law Shalu Minocha as the alleged conspirator. Shalu was arrested along with them. Police had initially suspected that she had hired the killers for Rs 6 lakh.The investigation, however, took a different turn after police questioned the three accused during their 24-hour custody. Investigators said call records showed more than 300 conversations between Subrat and Vishal, the highest number among the contacts examined in the case.Police also found that Vishal had obtained a new SIM card on September 3, two days before the murder, and allegedly made his first call from the new number to Subrat. Investigators also recovered deleted chats between the two and said their locations had coincided at several points before the killing.Police alleged that Subrat and Vishal had attempted to divert suspicion towards Shalu. Vishal reportedly told investigators that Subrat had asked him to kill his father and promised him Rs 6 lakh. He also allegedly claimed that Subrat had instructed him to name Shalu if the conspiracy was uncovered.Police are verifying these allegations through call records, digital evidence and other material. Commissioner of police Raghubir Lal said Subrat had not confessed to the murder and that all scientific, digital, CCTV, call-detail and circumstantial evidence would be independently scrutinised.The latest developments have also put Shalu’s alleged role under fresh scrutiny. Police said they had so far not found sufficient corroborative evidence establishing her involvement, though she has not been given a clean chit.“Whether she is complicit or not will be decided by the court,” a senior police officer said.Investigators have also recovered a duplicate key to Vineet’s flat from Vishal. Police said blood-stained clothes allegedly worn during the crime were recovered from a spot near Kanpur railway station.Police said the probe report submitted before the court would incorporate the latest findings and evidence gathered during the investigation.
Article Summary: Vineet Minocha, 63, was stabbed 26 times at his apartment in Kanpur. His son Subrat, 34, has been arrested for allegedly conspiring to murder his father. Police allege that Subrat had accumulated debts of more than Rs 40 lakh through gambling and IPL betting.

Article Title: ‘If police turn predator, what can one do’: MLA after 2 cops, 2 CRPF men held for ‘gang-rape’ at his UP farmhouse
Article Text:
MLA Umesh Sharma, who owns the farmhouse, claimed he was not present during the incident

What caretaker told police

Woman's allegation





AMROHA: “If the police department turns predator, what can one do?” asked Uttarakhand MLA Umesh Sharma while responding to allegations that four policemen, including two CRPF personnel, allegedly gang-raped a 25-year-old woman at his farmhouse in Amroha’s Hasanpur area.The four accused — CRPF inspector Lalaram Yadav, CRPF head constable Mohit Singh, Uttar Pradesh Police sub-inspector Sanjay Tomar and constable Pramod — were arrested after the woman approached police alleging that she was sexually assaulted at the farmhouse on Monday night.The farmhouse, owned by Sharma, who is the MLA from Khanpur in Uttarakhand’s Haridwar district, is located on the Atrasi-Hasanpur road. According to the police complaint, the group allegedly entered the property after threatening the caretaker.Reacting to the allegations on social media, Sharma said he was not present at the farmhouse when the incident allegedly occurred. He said he was in Landhora, Khanpur, attending a roadshow and a public programme from 6.30pm to 11pm and claimed that evidence of his presence was available on social media.The MLA also questioned how a caretaker could have prevented police personnel from entering the property. “If a local thana’s police officer comes with two CRPF personnel, will not the caretaker open the gates? What options does he have?” he said.Sharma added, “And if the police department turns predator, what can one do?”The farmhouse caretaker, Ramniwas, told police that he received several calls from a person identified as Parvinder, who allegedly told him that SSI Naresh Rana had arranged accommodation at the property for officials from the Union home ministry who were supposedly visiting for an inquiry.Ramniwas said Rana also contacted him and asked him to send the farmhouse location through WhatsApp.According to his statement, when he reached the farmhouse at around 10.13pm, he found Sanjay Tomar, a police constable, a CRPF inspector and a CRPF head constable at the property, along with a woman.Ramniwas said he asked the group to speak to the owner before entering the farmhouse. He alleged that Tomar abused and threatened him, saying he could be killed or sent to jail. Fearing the threats, the caretaker said he left the property.According to the woman's complaint, she had travelled from Fatehabad in Haryana to Amroha after an acquaintance invited her to visit religious sites.She allegedly met CRPF head constable Mohit Singh in Sonipat on Monday. The two then travelled to Meerut, where they picked up CRPF inspector Lalaram Yadav before travelling to Hasanpur.At Hasanpur, they allegedly met Sanjay Tomar, who was posted at Hasanpur police station.The woman alleged that after they reached the farmhouse, constable Pramod brought food and liquor. She told police that Mohit, Lalaram and Sanjay subsequently sexually assaulted her.She alleged that when Pramod later attempted to assault her, she pushed him away and locked herself inside a room. She then called police at around 6am on Tuesday.Amroha SP Lakhan Singh Yadav confirmed that an FIR had been registered under Section 70(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for gang rape and that all four accused had been taken into custody.Tomar and Pramod have been suspended, with a departmental inquiry initiated against them. Disciplinary proceedings against the two CRPF personnel have been forwarded to their respective unit headquarters.The woman was sent for a medical examination on Thursday, and police have recorded her statement.Police records show that Mohit is a head constable with the CRPF's 5th Battalion in Delhi, while Lalaram Yadav is an inspector with the 156th Battalion stationed in New Bongaigaon, Assam.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand MLA Umesh Sharma claims he was not present during the incident. Four policemen, including two CRPF personnel, allegedly gang-raped a 25-year-old woman at his farmhouse in Amroha’s Hasanpur area. The farmhouse, owned by Sharma, is located on the Atrasi-Hasanpur road.

Article Title: Speeding truck rams parked vehicles on Rajkot-Morbi highway; 2 killed, 3 hurt
Article Text:
A tragic incident occurred on the Rajkot-Morbi highway when a speeding truck crashed into parked vehicles.





RAJKOT: A late-night halt for tea and a break during travel ended in tragedy on the Rajkot-Morbi highway on Wednesday, when a speeding truck crashed into a parked car and autorickshaw near Hadala village, killing two men and injuring three others.Police identified the deceased as Azizshah Shahmadar, 45, a resident of Manharpara, and Kana Humbal, 24, of Bedi village. Both men were declared dead soon after an ambulance reached the spot. The injured were shifted to Rajkot Civil Hospital.According to police, the car and autorickshaw were parked on the roadside when the truck approached at high speed and crashed into them.Humbal had stopped at Momai Hotel with an acquaintance for tea and refreshments. He was sitting inside the car while his friends had stepped away to buy snacks.Shahmadar, who drove an autorickshaw to support his family, was going to Morbi with his son for a religious function. They halted near the hotel and his son had stepped out to make a purchase when the truck hit the autorickshaw.Humbal was the only brother to five sisters and was related to singers Meera Ahir and Vaishali Ahir.The truck driver fled after the crash. Police later arrested him and impounded his vehicle near Tankara in Morbi district.Officials said CCTV footage shows the truck approaching the parked vehicles at high speed before hitting them.
Article Summary: A speeding truck crashed into a parked car and autorickshaw near Hadala village, killing two men and injuring three others. Police identified the deceased as Azizshah Shahmadar, 45, a resident of Manharpara, and Kana Humbal, 24, of Bedi village.

Article Title: ‘She is in Tihar jail’: How drunk boast ‘I killed my wife’ cracked 15-month-old ‘lady don’ murder mystery
Article Text:
Mintu Choudhary alias Seema Choudhary (41), with 11 cases filed against her, had been reported missing by her son Hari Om Choudhary (20) on July 21 last year.

Anatomy of murder





JAIPUR: A boast made after a drinking session to an acquaintance about killing his wife and hiding her body eventually travelled to police, helping crack a 15-month-old disappearance case of a “lady don” in Jaipur.DCP (South) Rajarshi Raj Varma said Thursday that Muhana police arrested Mintu Choudhary’s husband and son after recovering her decomposed remains from a deep, dry well near Achrawala village.Mintu Choudhary alias Seema Choudhary (41), with 11 cases filed against her, had been reported missing by her son Hari Om Choudhary (20) on July 21 last year — nearly two months after she allegedly disappeared on May 27.Her phone had been switched off and the family had told relatives that they could not trace her.The breakthrough came when police received information that Mintu had not disappeared but had allegedly been murdered by Hari Om and his father Lala Ram Choudhary (42) about 15 months earlier.Investigators then questioned the two separately and, police said, they disclosed that her body had been dumped in a well outside Achrawala village.According to Varma, Mintu was killed and her body wrapped in a blanket before being transported in an auto at night and dumped into the well.The accused allegedly chose the isolated, dry well to conceal the body and avoid detection.“What initially helped them maintain the deception was a series of conflicting explanations about Mintu’s whereabouts. When relatives asked about her, the accused allegedly claimed first that she was in Tihar Jail and later that she had been lodged in Bharatpur Jail.Her sister contacted jail authorities and found that Mintu was not lodged in either facility,” Varma said, adding that Hari Om later allegedly approached police with a missing-person report (MPR), which police now suspect was an attempt by the duo to distance themselves from her disappearance.Varma said that the motive of the crime appeared to be “family tensions.”Police said the crucial information emerged during the subsequent investigation. Lala had allegedly consumed liquor one day and boasted to an acquaintance that he killed his wife and successfully concealed the crime. The information was passed on to others before reaching the police.The disclosure led investigators to focus on Hari Om and Lala Ram. Technical investigation and information from informers were used to corroborate the leads before the two were detained and questioned, police said.
Article Summary: Police arrested Mintu Choudhary’s husband and son after recovering her decomposed remains from a deep, dry well near Achrawala village. Her phone had been switched off and the family had told relatives that they could not trace her. The breakthrough came when police received information that Mintu had not disappeared but had allegedly been murdered.

Article Title: Koppal Gavi Mutt Pontiff to inaugurate Dasara 2026
Article Text:
Abhinava Gavisiddheshwar Mahaswami is the 18th pontiff and assumed charge in 2002.





BENGALURU: Koppal Gavi Mutt pontiff, who’s won accolades as water-conservation warrior and social-welfare sage, will inaugurate the 2026 edition of 10-day Mysuru Dasara festivities starting on Oct 11.Chief minister DK Shivakumar informed the legislative assembly Thursday Abhinava Gavishiddheshwar Mahaswami, 49, has accepted the govt’s invitation. He said, “I spoke to the seer on Thursday morning and requested him to declare the state festival open.”The choice brings a prominent spiritual and social figure from North Karnataka to the centre of the state’s biggest cultural celebration. The Dasara concludes on Oct 21 with a grand Vijayadashami parade.Abhinava Gavishiddheshwar Mahaswami is the 18th pontiff and assumed charge in 2002. His ‘Jala Deekshe’ campaign in North Karnataka focused on reviving and desilting lakes and addressing severe water scarcity. Under his leadership, the mutt has continued its work in education, food and spiritual service, including providing free boarding and educational support to students from rural and economically disadvantaged backgrounds.Koppal Gavi Mutt is known for the annual Gavisiddheshwara Jatre, popularly called ‘Ajjana Jatre’, one of the region’s largest religious gatherings. The mutt has traditionally used the occasion to recognise achievers from different walks of life.The selection of the seer for Mysuru Dasara comes after several names were discussed for the prestigious inauguration. Former cricketers Anil Kumble and Rahul Dravid, Supreme Court judge Justice BV Nagarathna and Karnataka High Court judge M Nagaprasanna were among the names doing the rounds.
Article Summary: Abhinava Gavishiddheshwar Mahaswami is the 18th pontiff and assumed charge in 2002. His campaign in North Karnataka focused on reviving and desilting lakes and addressing severe water scarcity. The selection of the seer for Mysuru Dasara comes after several names were discussed for the prestigious inauguration.

Article Title: 'Bunked classes, borrowed friend’s car': Days after BMW plunge, Navi Mumbai teen’s Honda City skids 70ft down hill, tells the tale
Article Text:
A 17-year-old boy named Chinmay Patil lost control of a Honda City while driving on Parsik Hill.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 17-year-old boy driving a Honda City lost control while negotiating a turn atop Parsik Hill in Belapur Thursday afternoon, sending the car skidding down the slope from a height of around 70 feet before it landed on Belapur-Uran railway tracks near the exit of a tunnel around 3.30pm.Patil suffered minor head injuries after the car somersaulted. Police said the airbags opened and he was thrown onto the rear seat. The incident comes days after a BMW crashed through a Coastal Road ramp and plunged 70ft, killing three college students.The teenager, Chinmay Patil, was taken to MGM Hospital where he received sutures and was discharged, police said. Patil, an HSC student at a Sanpada college and a resident of Sector 22, Turbhe, had bunked classes Thursday and borrowed a friend's Honda City to visit Parsik Hill, said inspector Lakhan Raskar of CBD-Belapur police station."He had parked the car near Sant Shri Vishavnath Maharaj Samadhi atop the hill. Around 3.30pm, while turning to leave, he accidentally accelerated instead of applying the brakes and lost control. The car then skidded down the slope and landed near the tunnel exit on the railway tracks."Swapnil Nila, chief PRO, Central Railway, said, "Due to the car landing on the Belapur-Uran railway track near the tunnel, only one train towards Uran got stranded, as train frequency is less on this harbour route." Arun Pawar, senior inspector, CBD-Belapur police, said the car owner would be summoned and legal action would be taken for allegedly allowing a minor to drive the vehicle.
Article Summary: 17-year-old Chinmay Patil lost control of a Honda City while driving on Parsik Hill. The car skidded down the slope from a height of around 70 feet before it landed on Belapur-Uran railway tracks near the exit of a tunnel. Patil suffered minor head injuries after the car somersaulted.

Article Title: BJP’s Fatehabad MLA Chhote Lal Verma dies at Noida hospital
Article Text:
MLA from Agra’s Fatehabad assembly constituency, Chhote Lal Verma





AGRA: BJP MLA from Agra’s Fatehabad assembly constituency, Chhote Lal Verma (68) died at a Noida hospital on Thursday evening while undergoing treatment.Verma had been suffering from fever for the past two days and was initially admitted to a private hospital in Agra after his condition deteriorated. As there was no significant improvement, his family decided to take him to Yatharth Hospital in Noida, where he died during treatment. Family sources said he suffered a cardiac arrest.The news of his death triggered an outpouring of grief among his supporters and BJP workers in Agra and Fatehabad.A former UP govt minister, Verma had represented Fatehabad constituency for the fourth time. The UP assembly’s official profile also records that he was elected to the House for a fourth term in 2022.UP CM Yogi Adityanath condoled his death in a post on X, describing it as “extremely heartbreaking” and offering prayers for the departed soul and strength to the bereaved family.
Article Summary: BJP MLA from Agra’s Fatehabad assembly constituency, Chhote Lal Verma (68) died at a Noida hospital on Thursday evening while undergoing treatment. Verma had been suffering from fever for the past two days. Family sources said he suffered a cardiac arrest.

Article Title: Bhupinder Singh Hooda slams lathicharge on farmers, questions crop procurement in Haryana
Article Text:
Bhupinder Singh Hooda said the use of force against farmers was unacceptable





ROHTAK: Former Haryana chief minister and Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Wednesday strongly condemned the reported lathicharge on farmers in Kurukshetra, alleging that the BJP government in the state was not working in the interests of farmers and was instead “harassing” them.Hooda said farmers were facing difficulties in selling their produce as procurement at government mandis was yet to pick up, while private buyers were purchasing the crop at significantly lower rates.“The government claims that bajra will be procured at Rs 2,900 per quintal, but procurement has not started properly. In the private market, farmers are being forced to sell it for around Rs 1,800 to Rs 1,900 per quintal,” Hooda said.He alleged that farmers were also facing difficulties in the procurement of paddy and were being forced to wait at grain markets with their produce.“Farmers are sitting distressed in the mandis because their crops are not being procured on time,” Hooda said, adding that the government needed to ensure timely procurement and payment to farmers.Strongly condemning the alleged lathicharge in Kurukshetra, Hooda said the use of force against farmers was unacceptable and accused the state government of failing to address their genuine concerns.He also alleged that farmers were not receiving essential agricultural inputs such as urea and DAP fertilisers on time, forcing them to make repeated rounds of supply centres.“This government is not farmer-friendly. Farmers are being troubled at every step. They do not get urea and DAP on time, procurement of crops is not taking place properly and they are being forced to sell their produce at lower prices in the private market,” Hooda alleged.Hooda said the government should immediately ensure uninterrupted procurement of farmers’ produce at the announced rates and make adequate supplies of fertilisers available ahead of the sowing season.His remarks came amid his ongoing public outreach in Garhi Sampla-Kiloi, where he has been meeting villagers and raising issues concerning farmers, the electoral process and the functioning of the state government.Earlier, Hooda had announced that the Haryana Congress would stage a protest outside the State Election Commission office in Chandigarh, alleging irregularities in the electoral process.Meanwhile, Rohtak Zila Parishad chairperson and BJP candidate from Garhi Sampla-Kiloi in the 2024 Haryana Assembly elections, Manju Hooda, had criticised Bhupinder Singh Hooda’s week-long public outreach in the constituency, claiming that it reflected his “weakening political hold” in the area.Manju Hooda alleged that the Congress’s support base in the constituency was declining and that the former chief minister was therefore having to reach out to voters village by village.
Article Summary: Former Haryana chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda strongly condemned the reported lathicharge on farmers in Kurukshetra. Hooda said farmers were facing difficulties in selling their produce as procurement at government mandis was yet to pick up. He accused the state government of failing to address their genuine concerns.

Article Title: UP man kills father with brick, axe over money dispute, goes to sleep after attack
Article Text:
Deceased Nawab Ali (L)





KANPUR: Police arrested a man for allegedly killing his 84-year-old father with a brick and an axe following a dispute over money in Para Ojhi village in Hamirpur’s Sadar Kotwali area on Wednesday night.Police said Ramzan allegedly attacked Nawab Ali, causing serious injuries to his head and face, after their dispute escalated. Nawab Ali was found dead on a cot inside the house on Thursday morning, while Ramzan had gone to sleep after the attack.Nawab Ali lived with his two sons. His elder son, Shamsuddin, is the gram pradhan, while Ramzan is the younger son. Family members said Ramzan had been ill and needed money for treatment and other expenses. He had been trying to secure a loan and had sought money from his father.Ramzan had also spoken to Shamsuddin about the loan three to four days earlier. Tension over money had persisted in the family since then.Shamsuddin informed police after the body was discovered. Villagers gathered at the house, where a blood-stained guma was found near the scene. Injuries were visible on Nawab Ali’s head and near his eye.CO Sadar Yashpal Singh and Additional Superintendent of Police Arvind Kumar Verma inspected the scene and questioned family members and villagers.A field unit collected possible evidence, while a dog squad examined the surrounding area.Police took the body into custody for post-mortem examination after completing panchanama proceedings. An FIR was being registered on the basis of the family’s complaint.Singh said the preliminary investigation indicated a dispute over a money transaction. He said further action would be based on the post-mortem report and facts emerging from the investigation.
Article Summary: Nawab Ali was found dead on a cot inside the house on Thursday morning. His elder son, Shamsuddin, is the gram pradhan, while Ramzan is the younger son. Ramzan allegedly attacked Nawab Ali, causing serious injuries to his head and face.

Article Title: Veeramani POCSO case: All-woman SIT formed to investigate against granite baron
Article Text:
Chennai police have established a Special Investigation Team to probe allegations of sexual offences against R Veeramani.





CHENNAI: Chennai police have formed an all-woman four-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the child rape case against the granites baron, R Veeramani, and other associated issues.The SIT will be headed by additional commissioner of police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch in Chennai city police. The other members are: Joint commissioner (west zone) N Disha Mittal, Superintendent of Police Mutharasi, who is spokesperson and media relations, and deputy commissioner of the Central Women and Children (CWC) unit Geethanjali.The team was formed as the investigation into the case expanded following the arrest of Veeramani and his associates. Police have been examining evidence and statements collected during the investigation, including digital material linked to the case.Veeramani was arrested along with Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan in Aug 29 in connection with a child rape case. A former employee of Gem Granites, Ganesan, was subsequently arrested after police found a video linked to the case on his mobile phone on Sep 22. Investigators were examining how he obtained the video and why he did not report it to the police.The SIT will coordinate the investigation and examine the evidence and statements collected so far as part of the continuing probe.
Article Summary: Chennai police have formed an all-woman Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the child rape case against granites baron, R Veeramani. The SIT will be headed by additional commissioner of police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch in Chennai city police.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.
